title: Trans flag heart in cross-stitch
subtitle: A heart filled with the transgender pride flag stripes on 14-count Aida
excerpt: A trans flag heart is a 65-by-60 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. The heart shape is filled with the five horizontal stripes of the transgender pride flag, light blue, pink, white, pink, light blue, using three floss colours. Finished size is about 12 x 11 cm in a 15 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. The transgender pride flag was designed by Monica Helms in 1999.

content.text: A trans flag heart is a 65-by-60 stitch piece on 14-count
. The heart silhouette is filled with the five equal horizontal stripes of the transgender pride flag: light blue at the outer edges, pink inward, and white at the centre. Three
colours cover the whole piece. Each stripe is twelve stitches deep. All stitches are full crosses, the stepped top of the heart shape gives a clean profile with no fractional stitches required.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white
items.substitutions: Pale grey Aida gives the white stripe more definition

content.text: Find the centre of the fabric. The chart centre falls on the central white stripe. Begin there with blanc and work the white stripe row across its full width within the heart silhouette.
Work the pink stripes above and below the white band (963), then the light blue stripes at the outer edges (3325). Keeping the stripe rows horizontal and straight is the key technical challenge.
The heart silhouette steps in and out along the sides. Follow the chart precisely on the stepped edges so each stripe colour aligns with the correct row.
Wash gently and press face-down until the stitches sit smooth and flat. Display in the hoop on a wall or trim and frame under glass. A white mount and light wood frame keeps the palette clean.

items.symptom: The stripe colours bleed into each other at the edges
items.cause: The transition row between stripes was worked in the wrong colour order.
items.fix: Work each stripe as a complete horizontal band from left to right before moving to the next. The boundary row should be a clean straight line. Once the stripe is in, check the left and right edges are at the same counted row before starting the next colour.

items.symptom: The heart outline looks bumpy at the curves
items.cause: The curved top of the heart was stitched as a straight edge rather than following the stepped curve on the chart.
items.fix: The heart outline uses single-stitch stepping at the lobes. Count each step from the chart before stitching. The curve should read smooth from a normal viewing distance once the stepping is complete.

content.text: The bi pride banner and ace pride spade in this sub-category use the same stripe-fill approach with different colour families.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
